How the live try-on works

This demo runs the same pipeline a production virtual fitting room uses, entirely in the browser — no server, no uploads.

STEP 1

See the body

The camera feed is sent frame-by-frame to Google's MediaPipe Pose model, which returns 33 body landmarks — shoulders, hips, elbows, knees — with a confidence score for each, roughly 30 times a second.

STEP 2

Measure the torso

From the shoulder and hip landmarks the page computes your shoulder width, torso length, and the angle your shoulders are tilted at. Those three numbers become the garment's size, length, and rotation.

STEP 3

Fit the 3D shirt

Your GLB shirt is rendered by Three.js in a transparent WebGL layer over the video, anchored at the neckline and scaled and rotated to your torso every frame. Landmark smoothing keeps it steady, so it follows you as you move instead of jittering. The model is unrigged, so the fit is rigid — true draping would need it rigged to a body skeleton.

Taking it to production

  • Real cloth warping: swap the flat overlay for a warping model (e.g. VITON-HD, HR-VITON, or a hosted try-on API) that bends the fabric around the body's shape and lighting.
  • Body segmentation: a segmentation mask (MediaPipe Selfie Segmentation) lets sleeves pass behind arms and hair fall over the collar, instead of the garment sitting on top of everything.
  • Size recommendation: shoulder width + torso length in pixels, calibrated against a known reference, maps to real garment measurements and a suggested size.
  • Garment prep: product photos need a clean front view with the background removed; transparent PNGs drop straight into this demo's Upload button.
Tip: plain background behind you Tip: good, even lighting Tip: fitted clothing tracks best Tip: keep hips in frame
